The road crossing where nature, signage, and corporate language first collide. The route gate is where polished assurance meets wet bark, old stone, and a forest that has not signed anything. The route gate is bureaucracy wedged between trees: a tiny official station trying to impose straight lines on a forest that only understands curves. The place breaks into usable table spaces: Queue lane: Wagons line up between rope posts and roots. Stamp shed: A cramped shed holds ledgers, lanterns, and a desk built around a branch. Bypass deer path: A narrow animal trail skirts the official lane. Inspection stump: A huge cut stump has become the inspection counter. Plants and materials: roots buckle the queue stones, moss softens every official post, vines steal loose paper overnight. Animals and background life: fox-bats nest above the stamp shed, small root mice chew wax seals, lark-moths orbit lanterns during delays. The air carries stamp echo, rope creak, wet paper...
